# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b72 — Resume a running thermostat without switching it OFF

**Fixes:** Home Assistant Resume / "Έλεγχος · Επαλήθευση και συνέχιση" erroneously demanded that previously controller-owned physical equipment be manually turned OFF before the controller could resume. For a radiator already heating normally, that enforced unnecessary interruption, reset the five-minute startup timer and recorded a fresh minimum-OFF baseline regardless of the actual physical OFF history.

## Correct Resume behavior

- **Already ON, previously controlled:** A user-requested Resume revalidates the exact original source identity, physical output state, native power permission and competing owners. It keeps the confirmed ownership record, original physical running timestamp, minimum-ON and maximum-ON limits, and does **not** call climate/switch power services.
- **Already ON, previously unowned:** ONLY an explicit Resume (never a background poll) may accept the running native endpoint after device/area registry, supported mode and current per-device power authorization checks. The controller begins a conservative supervised runtime interval without pretending it itself switched ON the appliance. Automatic/PID can then continue with the real room demand.
- **Already OFF:** Resume clears the stale pause, but records the observed physical OFF time rather than restarting the minimum OFF interval from the button click. Normal demand, native dwell and protection checks still determine when heat/cool may actually start.
- **Manual -> PID/Automatic:** When a user explicitly selects Manual from a previously selected PID or Automatic method, that previous mode is saved on the same controller. Pressing Resume after the manual intervention restores that actually remembered method and resumes evaluation. If no prior mode was ever saved (for example a Manual setting made in an older beta), Resume does not guess the previous choice. Select PID/Automatic once if necessary.
- **External supply switch ON:** Its existing recorded ownership is kept if it was already owned. An already-ON user-operated plug is never claimed, toggled or turned OFF just because Resume was pressed.
- **Supply OFF / downstream unavailable:** An intentionally unpowered native appliance can be reconciled as OFF without fabricating native capabilities; the existing demand-gated cold-start path remains responsible for any later power-on.
- **Pending uncertain commands:** Interrupted or unacknowledged physical commands still fail closed. An observed, explicitly commanded prior operation may be acknowledged, but its physical state must match the exact stored expected value. Missing source identity, competing owners, unauthorized methods, unsupported modes and state changes during the durable write still reject Resume.

## Implementation

The resume button makes **zero physical service calls**, retains existing minimum ON/OFF hardware protection, native defrost and shutdown restrictions, and schedules one normal controller evaluation instead of enforcing a new synthetic five-minute startup warmup.

Normal control remains governed by the **actual selected** method, targets, occupancy, sleep, windows, exact source and power-supply identity, and command acknowledgements. A radiator may still switch OFF later when the controller's legitimate measured demand or maximum-runtime protection requires it—not because of the Resume click itself.

This release retains Beta70's profile-aware PID scheduling and Beta71's restart-safe window handling. Existing per-cover lux options, WAQI AQI recognition, translations and update-coalescing safeguards are unchanged. The canonical integration stays `environment_manager`.

## Automated verification

CI executes the **real EquipmentRuntime.async_resume** method in isolated Home Assistant simulations, including owned and unowned running heat, Manual->PID restoration, physical OFF history, ON/OFF upstream supplies, committed vs unresolved native/supply commands, conflicting foreign owners and a physical state change while persistence yields. It asserts no actuator service is called.

The publisher also runs Beta61–71 native, PID, sleep/window, climate, AQI, shade/lux regressions plus actual HA dispatcher and Chromium load tests before publishing an unchanged, versioned ZIP. **Real hardware operation on a running thermostat remains to be checked.**

## Installation

Update the **existing** HACS Home Environment Manager custom integration to **v0.6.0b72**, restart Home Assistant and reload the dashboard. The manual ZIP contains `custom_components/environment_manager/` without renaming entities or deleting stored settings.
